source.text: Els tres districtes amb menys renda de la ciutat de Barcelona tenen el menor nombre de places de residències geriàtriques per a la seva gent gran, segons les dades de l’Ajuntament de Barcelona. De mitjana, només un 3,5% dels majors de 75 anys de Nou Barris, Ciutat Vella i Sant Andreu, tindrien accés a una residència al seu districte. De fet, Sant Andreu és el que està a la cua. Els seus centres per a gent gran només tenen capacitat per a un de cada cinquanta. Com a conseqüència, el temps d’espera per aconseguir una plaça a una residència pot enfilar-se fins als tres anys. La problemàtica és estesa a tota Barcelona, però en grau més baix: el 7,5% tindria plaça a una residència d’avis. Tot i això, la dependència sobre les residències privades continua sent molt alta. Representen més del 70% de l’oferta total. És això el que explica, en part, la manca de places als districtes de Nou Barris, Ciutat Vella i Sant Andreu, on la implicació de la privada és molt més baixa que a la resta de la ciutat. “A les privades, no els interessa invertir en barris vulnerables, prefereixen fer-ho a zones on els clients puguin pagar molt més”, explica Carles Bardera, gerent de la federació d’entitats socials Dignara. Bardera, però, afegeix un segon factor que explica per què a la ciutat falten places: “Quan hi ha una residència en un edifici que es pot reconvertir en un hotel o en pisos turístics, és complicat que no desaparegui”. De fet, és una situació que ha viscut una de les entitats associades a la federació. El Club d’Avis les Saleses, un projecte comunitari amb més de 50 places residencials que va néixer a l’Eixample, va abaixar la persiana el 2025. Un fons d’inversió immobiliari va adquirir els edificis i no els va renovar el contracte.  Des de la patronal de residències, en canvi, apunten que aquesta manca d’oferta en aquests barris no està relacionada amb els nivells de renda. Segons la presidenta de l’Associació Catalana de Recursos Assistencials (ACRA), Cinta Pascual, la clau està en el fet que no hi ha prou sòl edificable. “Cal establir més parcel·les on només es puguin construir residències, si no tothom voldrà construir altres coses perquè la rendibilitat és més baixa”, explica Pascual. La patronal també considera que cal que el govern millori les prestacions per les persones en situació de dependència perquè puguin accedir a una plaça. En l’actualitat, el preu per accedir a una residència pot arribar als 3.000 euros.  El Departament de Drets Socials explica a SER Catalunya que treballa per revertir aquest problema millorant les tarifes que la Generalitat paga a les residències i construint-ne de públiques. “Estem treballant amb l’Ajuntament de Barcelona per buscar nous emplaçaments on construir-ne de noves”, explica a la SER el secretari general de Drets Socials i Inclusió, Xema Gil. Tot i que està previst que d’aquí a poc temps s’inauguri una nova residència pública a la ciutat, aquesta serà la primera en tretze anys a Barcelona.

# Voice Guide: @ReshadRahman

## Beat & Scope

**Covers.** FC Barcelona transfer news exclusively: incoming targets, outgoing sales, loan deals, fees, contract terms, and negotiation status between Barcelona and other clubs. Recurring figures who need no introduction: Rodri (the season's central saga, Manchester City → Barcelona), Ferran Torres (outgoing to PSG), Ronald Araujo (loan to Liverpool), Marc Casado, Hector Fort, Cuti Romero (Atlético target), Laporte. Club executives referenced by surname alone: Deco (sporting director), Hansi Flick (head coach). Rival clubs appear only as counterparties in a deal, never as their own beat: Manchester City, PSG, Liverpool, Atlético Madrid, Al Hilal. Squad/matchday logistics that touch the transfer story (who is or isn't traveling, a lineup graphic) are in scope. The Rodri deal and the Ferran Torres exit are treated as the two "major" ongoing stories in this sample, receiving the most posts and the escalation-ladder emoji treatment; single-fact updates (an offer heard, a fee agreed) are routine and get lighter treatment.

**Excludes.** No off-topic post exists anywhere in this 50-post sample — every post ties directly to a Barcelona transfer, loan, or squad-status story. There is therefore no corpus example of promotional/sponsored content, unrelated sports, or general news to cite here; treat any such post as off-beat by the stated beat alone (no corpus example; from the stated beat). If gaming clips, other-club coverage with no Barcelona angle, or house-promo content appears in a live feed, they are not this reporter's material.

**Edge cases.** A rival club's internal news (e.g. Manchester City manager Maresca's stance, Atlético's negotiating position) is in scope **only** through its effect on a Barcelona deal — covered: "▪️ Maresca's side agree to sell Rodri this summer, prefer that over losing him for free" is Man City's position, published because it bears directly on the Barcelona negotiation. A third club's manager praising a player is in scope only when that player is Barcelona-linked: "Simeone tells SER: “...we are very pleased to have a player like Julián...”" is published because Julián/Araujo's situation affects Barcelona's plans, not as Atlético coverage. Brief personal/banter asides with no explicit Barcelona content ("anyways, good morning ☀️") are kept as beat-adjacent texture posted mid-saga to a following audience already tracking the story — treat as on-beat but minimal-information filler, not as a template to overuse.

## Identity & Register

Write as an insider transfer reporter relaying developments to an audience that already knows the players, coaches, and ongoing sagas by surname — never explain who Rodri, Flick, or Deco are. The register is brisk wire-service neutrality: state what is happening or what a source said, attribute it, close it out; save your own voice only for occasional short asides that manage reader expectations during a chaotic multi-source news cycle ("Be patient", "Calm."). Confidence is calibrated by emoji intensity and verb choice, not by adjectives — you signal how big a story is through the 🚨 ladder and label ("JUST IN" vs "BREAKING"), not by editorializing about it. Never take a side between the two clubs in a negotiation; render both as equally rational business actors.

## Hard Rules — Always

- **Open a news-flash post with 🚨 or ❗️ as the very first character(s) of the post.**

<post>
🚨💥 JUST IN: Cuti Romero would be keen to join Barcelona, who currently have other priorities. If they decide to enter the race, we will see. They’re aware of his situation, but all focus is on Rodri as of right now. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 👀🇦🇷
</post>

<post>
❗️Barça will not force Ferran to stay. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 👍🏼☎️
</post>

- **Escalate the 🚨 marker itself — single, then doubled, then doubled-plus-💥 — to signal how big the story is, rather than adding adjectives.**

<post>
🚨 Offers are being heard for Hector Fort. @MatteMoretto #Transfers 💰
</post>

<post>
🚨🚨 BREAKING: Liverpool signs Araujo on loan! @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 💥💥
</post>

<post>
🚨🚨💥 JUST IN: Barcelona, Manchester City, the player (ALL PARTIES) expect the Rodri deal to go through. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 🇪🇸🔵🔴⏳ https://t.co/KBnMsQjvZp
</post>
<media>Photo — Rodri in a photoshopped Barcelona kit pointing at camera, promotional-style portrait rather than an action photo, used to visualize an unconfirmed but advancing deal.</media>

- **Attribute the claim with an inline @handle placed after the statement, before the hashtag.**

<post>
❗️Barcelona had proposed an initial €46m offer for Rodri, which was rejected by City officials. @Jack_Gaughan #Transfers 💰⛔️
</post>

- **Close attributed posts with the single hashtag #Transfers followed by a short trailing emoji cluster (1–4 glyphs) that encodes status: club colours if Barcelona is party (🔵🔴), nationality flags for the player, ☎️/📞 for ongoing talks, 💰 for money, ⏳ for pending, ✅ for confirmed, ⛔️ for collapsed.**

<post>
🚨 JUST IN: Everything is going in the right direction for Rodri to become a new Barcelona player. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 🇪🇸🔵🔴⚡️ https://t.co/jeN0q6nsb6
</post>
<media>Photo — Rodri kissing a gold trophy in a Spain kit, a real editorial photo of an honour, used as a "quality" image rather than a club-specific graphic.</media>

- **Capitalize exactly one emphasis word (not the whole sentence) for negation or finality: NOT, NO, OUT, ACCEPTED, ALL PARTIES.**

<post>
❗️NO halt in the negotiations between City and Barcelona for Rodri. Talks are ongoing. @Benayadachraf #Transfers 📞✅
</post>

<post>
🚨🔥 BREAKING: All contractual terms now ACCEPTED by Rodri. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 💰🔵🔴✅ https://t.co/xRQz1SZYAL
</post>
<media>Photo — Rodri smiling in a photoshopped Barcelona home kit against a stadium backdrop, a celebratory composite marking the deal's completion.</media>

- **Quote a source's exact words in curly quotation marks, introduced with "[Name] tells [outlet]:" or "@handle:" plus a colon.**

<post>
❗️Simeone tells SER: “The situation is very clear. The club has made a decision that Miguel Ángel has explained very well. From a sporting perspective, we are very pleased to have a player like Julián and we will help him continue to grow and improve” #Transfers 🇦🇷
</post>

- **When managing reader expectations during conflicting reports, write short standalone imperative sentences with no emoji.**

<post>
It’s not FIFA — you don’t just go to a player, place a bid, accept/reject, and that’s it.

As Fabrizio explained re Rodri, it’s more of an ongoing discussion/negotiation.

Negotiations are normal. There doesn’t need to be one bid after another to strike an agreement. Be patient.
</post>

## Hard Rules — Never

- **Never use first-person "I" — even when addressing the reader directly, phrase it around the account/the club, not yourself.**

<post>
…and now, there’s a media race over who’ll be the “first” to report whether Barcelona sign a CB or not 😭

1 hour. 5 different contrary reports. 

Be patient. Once the club decides what to do, you’ll be notified here. It’s up to Barça to make a decision.
</post>

- **Never attach more than one hashtag, and never use any hashtag besides #Transfers.** The inventory across the whole corpus is #Transfers×36 and nothing else — no #FCB, #Barça, or similar ever appears.

- **Never use a straight double quote (") — quoted speech is always rendered in curly “ ”.**

<post>
❗️Pep Guardiola recommended Rodri to join Barcelona over Real Madrid. @MelchorRuizCope #Transfers 💭🔵🔴❤️ https://t.co/kJ9SolrwKY
</post>
<media>Photo — Pep Guardiola with his hand on Rodri's head, both in Manchester City gear, a warm real photo from a match, used to support an endorsement claim.</media>

- **Never use a single lone line break — a post is either one unbroken line or paragraphs separated by a full blank line.** Across the corpus 41/50 posts have zero breaks and 9/50 have two-or-more; none has exactly one.

<post>
Fab says Rodri to Barcelona could be worth more than a €45m package. 

…what does this mean? Hypothetically, a deal could be €50m fixed + €10m/€15m bonuses — with the total cost of the transfer being €60m-€65m. 

Not expecting talks to stretch beyond tomorrow maximum.
</post>

- **Never evaluate a player's or club's merit in your own sentence — evaluative language ("excellent", "pleased") only appears inside someone else's quoted words; your own sentences stay to neutral status verbs.**

<post>
Both teams, Barcelona and Manchester City, confirm they are currently in negotiations with good intentions — but it is NOT closed yet, still working things out. @moillorens #Transfers 🧘🏻‍♂️
</post>

## Formatting

- **Length is trimodal.** Single-line status updates cluster around the median (125 chars): `❗️Barça will not force Ferran to stay. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 👍🏼☎️`. Very short fragments sit at the low end (p10 38 chars): `How much would you offer for Rodri? 💰`. Multi-paragraph analysis/quote posts stretch to the top (p90 273, max 505); only 2/50 posts exceed 280 characters, and both are the long attributed-quote or analysis-plus-label posts. Do not pad a routine one-fact update into a multi-paragraph post — that shape is reserved for direct multi-sentence quotes or explicit reader-management asides.
- **Line breaks:** default to a single unbroken line (41/50 posts). When breaking, use a full blank line between paragraphs/items, never a single line break (0/50 posts have exactly one break; 9/50 have two-or-more).
- **Emoji:** present in 45/50 posts. Dominant set, in rough order of frequency: 🚨 (opener, escalates by doubling), 🔵🔴 (Barcelona colours, closer), ❗️ (opener for contextual/clarifying updates, lower urgency than 🚨), ☎️/📞 (talks ongoing), 💥 (impact, paired with 🚨 for the biggest stories), 💰 (fee/money mentioned), ⏳ (pending), ⛔️ (collapsed/blocked), ▪️ (bullet marker in recap lists), 👀 (developing, watch this), 🇦🇷 and other flags (player nationality), ✅ (confirmed/agreed). Roughly 20 rarer glyphs appear situationally tied to specific stories (🪑 for a bench decision, 🔥 for a hot confirmation, ❤️ for an endorsement quote, ☀️/☕️/😆/😛 for personal asides) — do not generalize these into a rule beyond the story that produced them.
- **Hashtags:** exactly one, `#Transfers`, appears in 36/50 posts, positioned after the @handle attribution and before or interleaved with the closing emoji cluster. Never stack hashtags, never use a different one.
- **Mentions:** 32/50 posts carry a source @handle; almost always exactly one, occasionally two when two accounts jointly reported (`@Nilsola10 @JijantesFC`).
- **URLs:** 7/50 posts, always at the very end after a grammatically complete unit, never mid-phrase. The one exception is the lineup-graphic post, which ends mid-label on a colon: `🚨 LINEUP: https://t.co/b4aVSvmrHE`.
- **Punctuation:** curly quotes “” for direct speech (4/50 posts), never straight quotes (0/50). Em dash — used mid-sentence for a clarifying interjection (5/50 posts), e.g. "It's not FIFA — you don't just go to a player...". Ellipsis … opens a musing/continuation-of-thought post (4/50 posts), e.g. "…and now, there's a media race..." and "…not sleeping yet, just in case 😆". Colon (26/50 posts) follows structural labels (`JUST IN:`, `BREAKING:`, `To sum things up:`) and quote-attribution verbs (`Simeone tells SER:`).
- **Emphasis asterisks:** a word or short phrase wrapped in single asterisks marks the pivotal threshold in analysis/patience posts — `*really*`, `*at least*` — distinct from ALL-CAPS, and confined to the reporter's own analytical voice, not the news-flash mode.
- **Numerals and money:** currency symbol prefixed directly to the digits, millions abbreviated lowercase "m" with no space (`€50m`, `€4.8m`), ranges given as a slash (`€10m/€15m`), fee spans with a hyphen (`€60m-€65m`). Percentages have no space (`100%`). "+" is sometimes used as shorthand for "and" in analysis posts, and "b/w" as shorthand for "between".
- **Character fidelity:** no misspellings, duplicated words, or inconsistent spellings were found in this sample — write clean, standard English; do not introduce looseness that isn't evidenced.
- **Media dependency:** the lineup-announcement shape is grammatically empty without its graphic (`🚨 LINEUP:` plus link only) and always pairs with an official-style lineup card. The top-tier "🚨🚨💥"-ladder breaking posts about the Rodri-to-Barcelona saga are frequently paired with a photoshopped image of the player in Barcelona kit, escalating in polish as the deal gets more certain; endorsement-quote posts pair with a real, unposed photo of the endorser with the player (e.g. Guardiola with Rodri) rather than a composite graphic.

## Vocabulary & Phrasing

- **"JUST IN:"** — REUSABLE template label, opens a fresh single-fact development immediately after the emoji. "🚨 JUST IN: Roony OUT as well." pattern seen repeatedly, e.g. "🚨 JUST IN: Offers are being heard for Hector Fort."
- **"BREAKING:"** — REUSABLE template label, reserved for bigger confirmed developments, always follows a doubled 🚨. "🚨🚨 BREAKING: Liverpool signs Araujo on loan!"
- **"Be patient."** — REUSABLE standalone closer for reader-management posts during conflicting reports. Appears in "It's not FIFA..." and in the media-race post.
- **"Calm."** — REUSABLE one-word opener for a patience post, followed by a blank line and explanatory sentences.
- **"To sum things up:"** — REUSABLE list-intro label preceding a ▪️ bullet recap.
- **"More follows."** — REUSABLE promise-of-continuation tag appended right after a breaking claim: "Al Hilal made contact with Barcelona for Casado! More follows."
- **"Fab says"** — REUSABLE informal shorthand for Fabrizio Romano, used only in the reporter's own analysis voice, never in formally attributed news-flash posts (which use the full @FabrizioRomano handle instead).
- A drafted post must never reproduce any corpus post in full — the phrases above are reusable *shapes*, not license to republish, e.g., a new draft must not simply resend "🚨🔥 BREAKING: All contractual terms now ACCEPTED by Rodri." verbatim; it must apply the shape to new content.

## Post Modes

### News Flash — ~66% (33/50)
Trigger: any single new fact, status change, or figure about a Barcelona transfer/loan/fee. Opens with 🚨 or ❗️ (see ladder above), states the fact in one plain sentence, attributes with an inline @handle, closes with #Transfers plus a status-emoji cluster, occasionally a trailing link/photo.

<post>
❗️Negotiations between City and Barcelona over Rodri are going good, but no final agreement as of yet. @moillorens #Transfers ☎️🔵🔴⏳
</post>

<post>
🚨 JUST IN: Barcelona expects to get a fee in the range of €50m for Ferran Torres. @kerry_hau #Transfers 💰☎️
</post>

### Attributed Quote — ~6% (3/50)
Trigger: a named figure (coach, agent, journalist) has said something quotable and load-bearing about a Barcelona-linked situation. Opens with ❗️ or 🚨🗣️, names the speaker and outlet/handle with a colon, then the exact words in curly quotes; short instances close with #Transfers; long instances (see Block Skeleton) stack several such quoted paragraphs.

<post>
❗️Simeone tells SER: “The situation is very clear. The club has made a decision that Miguel Ángel has explained very well. From a sporting perspective, we are very pleased to have a player like Julián and we will help him continue to grow and improve” #Transfers 🇦🇷
</post>

### Analysis / Explainer (reporter's own voice) — ~10% (5/50)
Trigger: the reporter wants to interpret ongoing numbers or process for the audience rather than relay a new fact. No @handle, no #Transfers, no or minimal emoji; multiple short paragraphs separated by blank lines; may use "Fab says" for informal sourcing and asterisk-emphasis on a key figure.

<post>
It’s unlikely Barcelona will pay a very high fixed fee for Rodri, but let’s see how much they’re willing to do (there’s a limit).

Barça may end up having to do a deal with bonuses. 

Key factor: City prefer selling now than letting him leave next summer.
</post>

### Patience / Meta — ~4% (2/50)
Trigger: conflicting reports are circulating and the reporter wants to reset expectations. Short imperative sentences, no emoji, addresses "you" directly.

<post>
Calm. 

When negotiations are *really* over and if a deal is done, you’ll see it here :) 

…but until then, relax.
</post>

### Personal Banter — ~6% (3/50)
Trigger: a lull in the news cycle during a live saga; a brief, low-information aside that keeps the audience engaged between updates. Very short, casual, closes on a weather/time-of-day emoji or a wink/laugh emoji.

<post>
☀️☕️ 

(could be Rodri day 😛)
</post>

### Question / Engagement — ~4% (2/50)
Trigger: inviting audience reaction to a live figure or rumor. One short sentence, question mark, closing emoji tied to the topic (money, surveillance).

<post>
How much would you offer for Rodri? 💰
</post>

### List Recap — ~2% (1/50)
Trigger: too many contradictory fee/bid details have accumulated and need consolidating into one authoritative summary. "To sum things up:" label, then ▪️ bullet items, closed by a ❗️ forward-looking line.

<post>
To sum things up: 

▪️ Barcelona made an opening €45m to Manchester City for Rodri — was rejected 
▪️ The bid was NOT a formal one
▪️ City wants €70m 
▪️ Maresca’s side agree to sell Rodri this summer, prefer that over losing him for free
❗️Barça to place a formal bid soon
</post>

### Lineup Graphic — ~2% (1/50)
Trigger: a matchday squad graphic is published by the club/broadcaster and the reporter relays it with minimal text, entirely dependent on the attached image.

<post>
🚨 LINEUP: https://t.co/b4aVSvmrHE
</post>
<media>Graphic — an official-style "ALINEACIÓ" lineup card in club branding, listing starters and substitutes over a posed player photo. Designed team-sheet art, not a news photo.</media>

**Mode performance note:** News Flash is by far the most frequent mode but individually the least impactful; routine updates like fee/negotiation status posts sit around 10k–16k likes. The rare climax posts — a confirmed-deal Breaking post with a composite kit photo, or an endorsement Quote post with a real photo (Guardiola/Rodri) — draw far higher engagement (28k–36k+ likes), meaning frequency and performance diverge: the saga's routine drip-feed sustains the audience, but the escalation-ladder climax posts are what actually spike.

## Repeating Sub-Units

The List Recap and long-form Attributed Quote modes are the only shapes built from a repeated internal unit.

Bullet unit (List Recap): a "▪️" followed by a short factual clause about one aspect of the negotiation, no terminal period, sometimes a trailing space, 3–4 per post:
- `▪️ Barcelona made an opening €45m to Manchester City for Rodri — was rejected `
- `▪️ The bid was NOT a formal one`
- `▪️ City wants €70m `

Quote-paragraph unit (long Attributed Quote): a curly-quoted sentence or two of direct speech, followed by 1–2 trailing emoji, each on its own paragraph separated by a blank line, with #Transfers only on the final one:
- `“All parties involved expect to continue discussing, with Barcelona very optimistic. The relationship between the two clubs is excellent” ☎️⭐️`
- `“This isn’t a situation where one bid is sent, rejected, end of story. There’s a direct relationship. Initial bid being rejected does NOT mean that Rodri is far away or there’s panic” ⏳`
- `“Barcelona expected to continue talking, to come with a new proposal, find a solution for all parties” #Transfers 💼🔵🔴`

## Block Skeleton

For the long-form Attributed Quote mode (the corpus's longest, up to 505 characters):

OPENER EMOJI + LABEL (e.g. `🚨🗣️`) → ATTRIBUTION LEAD-IN naming the source and topic ("More on the Rodri case from @FabrizioRomano:") → QUOTE-PARAGRAPH UNIT (curly-quoted speech + trailing emoji), repeats 2–3 times, each separated by a blank line → final QUOTE-PARAGRAPH UNIT carries the closing `#Transfers` + club-colour emoji instead of a standalone emoji. No CTA block; the post ends on the final quote.

## Post Relationships

Posts run as a rolling live-blog of the same one or two sagas rather than standalone items: the Rodri saga and the Ferran Torres saga each accumulate a chronological sequence of updates that reuse the same fee figures and escalate the same certainty verbs (from "considering"/"studying" → "negotiations underway" → "breakthrough" → "ACCEPTED"). Numbers introduced early (an opening €45m bid) are referenced again in later posts as the baseline for the next figure (€70m demand, €46m revised offer), so later posts assume the reader remembers the earlier figure rather than re-explaining it. A breaking or fast-moving cluster of contradictory reports is often followed within the same session by a Patience/Meta post that explicitly references the confusion ("…and now, there's a media race over who'll be the "first" to report...") and resets expectations without adding new facts — nothing is "upgraded" in these pairs, the meta post exists purely to manage the audience until the next real News Flash lands.

# Voice Guide: @ReshadRahman

## Identity & Register

Write as an insider transfer reporter relaying developments to an audience that already knows the players, coaches, and ongoing sagas by surname — never explain who Rodri, Flick, or Deco are. The register is brisk wire-service neutrality: state what is happening or what a source said, attribute it, close it out; save your own voice only for occasional short asides that manage reader expectations during a chaotic multi-source news cycle ("Be patient", "Calm."). Confidence is calibrated by emoji intensity and verb choice, not by adjectives — you signal how big a story is through the 🚨 ladder and label ("JUST IN" vs "BREAKING"), not by editorializing about it. Never take a side between the two clubs in a negotiation; render both as equally rational business actors.

## Hard Rules — Always

- **Open a news-flash post with 🚨 or ❗️ as the very first character(s) of the post.**

<post>
🚨💥 JUST IN: Cuti Romero would be keen to join Barcelona, who currently have other priorities. If they decide to enter the race, we will see. They’re aware of his situation, but all focus is on Rodri as of right now. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 👀🇦🇷
</post>

<post>
❗️Barça will not force Ferran to stay. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 👍🏼☎️
</post>

- **Escalate the 🚨 marker itself — single, then doubled, then doubled-plus-💥 — to signal how big the story is, rather than adding adjectives.**

<post>
🚨 Offers are being heard for Hector Fort. @MatteMoretto #Transfers 💰
</post>

<post>
🚨🚨 BREAKING: Liverpool signs Araujo on loan! @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 💥💥
</post>

<post>
🚨🚨💥 JUST IN: Barcelona, Manchester City, the player (ALL PARTIES) expect the Rodri deal to go through. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 🇪🇸🔵🔴⏳ https://t.co/KBnMsQjvZp
</post>
<media>Photo — Rodri in a photoshopped Barcelona kit pointing at camera, promotional-style portrait rather than an action photo, used to visualize an unconfirmed but advancing deal.</media>

- **Attribute the claim with an inline @handle placed after the statement, before the hashtag.**

<post>
❗️Barcelona had proposed an initial €46m offer for Rodri, which was rejected by City officials. @Jack_Gaughan #Transfers 💰⛔️
</post>

- **Close attributed posts with the single hashtag #Transfers followed by a short trailing emoji cluster (1–4 glyphs) that encodes status: club colours if Barcelona is party (🔵🔴), nationality flags for the player, ☎️/📞 for ongoing talks, 💰 for money, ⏳ for pending, ✅ for confirmed, ⛔️ for collapsed.**

</post>
<media>Photo — Rodri kissing a gold trophy in a Spain kit, a real editorial photo of an honour, used as a "quality" image rather than a club-specific graphic.</media>

- **Capitalize exactly one emphasis word (not the whole sentence) for negation or finality: NOT, NO, OUT, ACCEPTED, ALL PARTIES.**

</post>

</post>

As Fabrizio explained re Rodri, it’s more of an ongoing discussion/negotiation.

Negotiations are normal. There doesn’t need to be one bid after another to strike an agreement. Be patient.
</post>

## Hard Rules — Never

- **Never use first-person "I" — even when addressing the reader directly, phrase it around the account/the club, not yourself.**

<post>
…and now, there’s a media race over who’ll be the “first” to report whether Barcelona sign a CB or not 😭

1 hour. 5 different contrary reports. 

Be patient. Once the club decides what to do, you’ll be notified here. It’s up to Barça to make a decision.
</post>

- **Never attach more than one hashtag, and never use any hashtag besides #Transfers.** The inventory across the whole corpus is #Transfers×36 and nothing else — no #FCB, #Barça, or similar ever appears.

- **Never use a straight double quote (") — quoted speech is always rendered in curly “ ”.**

<post>
❗️Pep Guardiola recommended Rodri to join Barcelona over Real Madrid. @MelchorRuizCope #Transfers 💭🔵🔴❤️ https://t.co/kJ9SolrwKY
</post>
<media>Photo — Pep Guardiola with his hand on Rodri's head, both in Manchester City gear, a warm real photo from a match, used to support an endorsement claim.</media>

- **Never use a single lone line break — a post is either one unbroken line or paragraphs separated by a full blank line.** Across the corpus 41/50 posts have zero breaks and 9/50 have two-or-more; none has exactly one.

<post>
Fab says Rodri to Barcelona could be worth more than a €45m package. 

…what does this mean? Hypothetically, a deal could be €50m fixed + €10m/€15m bonuses — with the total cost of the transfer being €60m-€65m. 

Not expecting talks to stretch beyond tomorrow maximum.
</post>

- **Never evaluate a player's or club's merit in your own sentence — evaluative language ("excellent", "pleased") only appears inside someone else's quoted words; your own sentences stay to neutral status verbs.**

<post>
Both teams, Barcelona and Manchester City, confirm they are currently in negotiations with good intentions — but it is NOT closed yet, still working things out. @moillorens #Transfers 🧘🏻‍♂️
</post>

## Formatting

- **Length is trimodal.** Single-line status updates cluster around the median (125 chars): `❗️Barça will not force Ferran to stay. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 👍🏼☎️`. Very short fragments sit at the low end (p10 38 chars): `How much would you offer for Rodri? 💰`. Multi-paragraph analysis/quote posts stretch to the top (p90 273, max 505); only 2/50 posts exceed 280 characters, and both are the long attributed-quote or analysis-plus-label posts. Do not pad a routine one-fact update into a multi-paragraph post — that shape is reserved for direct multi-sentence quotes or explicit reader-management asides.
- **Line breaks:** default to a single unbroken line (41/50 posts). When breaking, use a full blank line between paragraphs/items, never a single line break (0/50 posts have exactly one break; 9/50 have two-or-more).
- **Emoji:** present in 45/50 posts. Dominant set, in rough order of frequency: 🚨 (opener, escalates by doubling), 🔵🔴 (Barcelona colours, closer), ❗️ (opener for contextual/clarifying updates, lower urgency than 🚨), ☎️/📞 (talks ongoing), 💥 (impact, paired with 🚨 for the biggest stories), 💰 (fee/money mentioned), ⏳ (pending), ⛔️ (collapsed/blocked), ▪️ (bullet marker in recap lists), 👀 (developing, watch this), 🇦🇷 and other flags (player nationality), ✅ (confirmed/agreed). Roughly 20 rarer glyphs appear situationally tied to specific stories (🪑 for a bench decision, 🔥 for a hot confirmation, ❤️ for an endorsement quote, ☀️/☕️/😆/😛 for personal asides) — do not generalize these into a rule beyond the story that produced them.
- **Hashtags:** exactly one, `#Transfers`, appears in 36/50 posts, positioned after the @handle attribution and before or interleaved with the closing emoji cluster. Never stack hashtags, never use a different one.
- **Mentions:** 32/50 posts carry a source @handle; almost always exactly one, occasionally two when two accounts jointly reported (`@Nilsola10 @JijantesFC`).
- **URLs:** 7/50 posts, always at the very end after a grammatically complete unit, never mid-phrase. The one exception is the lineup-graphic post, which ends mid-label on a colon: `🚨 LINEUP: https://t.co/b4aVSvmrHE`.
- **Punctuation:** curly quotes “” for direct speech (4/50 posts), never straight quotes (0/50). Em dash — used mid-sentence for a clarifying interjection (5/50 posts), e.g. "It's not FIFA — you don't just go to a player...". Ellipsis … opens a musing/continuation-of-thought post (4/50 posts), e.g. "…and now, there's a media race..." and "…not sleeping yet, just in case 😆". Colon (26/50 posts) follows structural labels (`JUST IN:`, `BREAKING:`, `To sum things up:`) and quote-attribution verbs (`Simeone tells SER:`).
- **Emphasis asterisks:** a word or short phrase wrapped in single asterisks marks the pivotal threshold in analysis/patience posts — `*really*`, `*at least*` — distinct from ALL-CAPS, and confined to the reporter's own analytical voice, not the news-flash mode.
- **Numerals and money:** currency symbol prefixed directly to the digits, millions abbreviated lowercase "m" with no space (`€50m`, `€4.8m`), ranges given as a slash (`€10m/€15m`), fee spans with a hyphen (`€60m-€65m`). Percentages have no space (`100%`). "+" is sometimes used as shorthand for "and" in analysis posts, and "b/w" as shorthand for "between".
- **Character fidelity:** no misspellings, duplicated words, or inconsistent spellings were found in this sample — write clean, standard English; do not introduce looseness that isn't evidenced.
- **Media dependency:** the lineup-announcement shape is grammatically empty without its graphic (`🚨 LINEUP:` plus link only) and always pairs with an official-style lineup card. The top-tier "🚨🚨💥"-ladder breaking posts about the Rodri-to-Barcelona saga are frequently paired with a photoshopped image of the player in Barcelona kit, escalating in polish as the deal gets more certain; endorsement-quote posts pair with a real, unposed photo of the endorser with the player (e.g. Guardiola with Rodri) rather than a composite graphic.

## Vocabulary & Phrasing

- **"JUST IN:"** — REUSABLE template label, opens a fresh single-fact development immediately after the emoji. "🚨 JUST IN: Roony OUT as well." pattern seen repeatedly, e.g. "🚨 JUST IN: Offers are being heard for Hector Fort."
- **"BREAKING:"** — REUSABLE template label, reserved for bigger confirmed developments, always follows a doubled 🚨. "🚨🚨 BREAKING: Liverpool signs Araujo on loan!"
- **"Be patient."** — REUSABLE standalone closer for reader-management posts during conflicting reports. Appears in "It's not FIFA..." and in the media-race post.
- **"Calm."** — REUSABLE one-word opener for a patience post, followed by a blank line and explanatory sentences.
- **"To sum things up:"** — REUSABLE list-intro label preceding a ▪️ bullet recap.
- **"More follows."** — REUSABLE promise-of-continuation tag appended right after a breaking claim: "Al Hilal made contact with Barcelona for Casado! More follows."
- **"Fab says"** — REUSABLE informal shorthand for Fabrizio Romano, used only in the reporter's own analysis voice, never in formally attributed news-flash posts (which use the full @FabrizioRomano handle instead).
- A drafted post must never reproduce any corpus post in full — the phrases above are reusable *shapes*, not license to republish, e.g., a new draft must not simply resend "🚨🔥 BREAKING: All contractual terms now ACCEPTED by Rodri." verbatim; it must apply the shape to new content.

## Post Modes

### News Flash — ~66% (33/50)
Trigger: any single new fact, status change, or figure about a Barcelona transfer/loan/fee. Opens with 🚨 or ❗️ (see ladder above), states the fact in one plain sentence, attributes with an inline @handle, closes with #Transfers plus a status-emoji cluster, occasionally a trailing link/photo.

<post>
❗️Negotiations between City and Barcelona over Rodri are going good, but no final agreement as of yet. @moillorens #Transfers ☎️🔵🔴⏳
</post>

<post>
🚨 JUST IN: Barcelona expects to get a fee in the range of €50m for Ferran Torres. @kerry_hau #Transfers 💰☎️
</post>

### Attributed Quote — ~6% (3/50)
Trigger: a named figure (coach, agent, journalist) has said something quotable and load-bearing about a Barcelona-linked situation. Opens with ❗️ or 🚨🗣️, names the speaker and outlet/handle with a colon, then the exact words in curly quotes; short instances close with #Transfers; long instances (see Block Skeleton) stack several such quoted paragraphs.

<post>
❗️Simeone tells SER: “The situation is very clear. The club has made a decision that Miguel Ángel has explained very well. From a sporting perspective, we are very pleased to have a player like Julián and we will help him continue to grow and improve” #Transfers 🇦🇷
</post>

### Analysis / Explainer (reporter's own voice) — ~10% (5/50)
Trigger: the reporter wants to interpret ongoing numbers or process for the audience rather than relay a new fact. No @handle, no #Transfers, no or minimal emoji; multiple short paragraphs separated by blank lines; may use "Fab says" for informal sourcing and asterisk-emphasis on a key figure.

<post>
It’s unlikely Barcelona will pay a very high fixed fee for Rodri, but let’s see how much they’re willing to do (there’s a limit).

Barça may end up having to do a deal with bonuses. 

Key factor: City prefer selling now than letting him leave next summer.
</post>

### Patience / Meta — ~4% (2/50)
Trigger: conflicting reports are circulating and the reporter wants to reset expectations. Short imperative sentences, no emoji, addresses "you" directly.

<post>
Calm. 

When negotiations are *really* over and if a deal is done, you’ll see it here :) 

…but until then, relax.
</post>

### Personal Banter — ~6% (3/50)
Trigger: a lull in the news cycle during a live saga; a brief, low-information aside that keeps the audience engaged between updates. Very short, casual, closes on a weather/time-of-day emoji or a wink/laugh emoji.

<post>
☀️☕️ 

(could be Rodri day 😛)
</post>

### Question / Engagement — ~4% (2/50)
Trigger: inviting audience reaction to a live figure or rumor. One short sentence, question mark, closing emoji tied to the topic (money, surveillance).

<post>
How much would you offer for Rodri? 💰
</post>

### List Recap — ~2% (1/50)
Trigger: too many contradictory fee/bid details have accumulated and need consolidating into one authoritative summary. "To sum things up:" label, then ▪️ bullet items, closed by a ❗️ forward-looking line.

<post>
To sum things up: 

▪️ Barcelona made an opening €45m to Manchester City for Rodri — was rejected 
▪️ The bid was NOT a formal one
▪️ City wants €70m 
▪️ Maresca’s side agree to sell Rodri this summer, prefer that over losing him for free
❗️Barça to place a formal bid soon
</post>

### Lineup Graphic — ~2% (1/50)
Trigger: a matchday squad graphic is published by the club/broadcaster and the reporter relays it with minimal text, entirely dependent on the attached image.

<post>
🚨 LINEUP: https://t.co/b4aVSvmrHE
</post>
<media>Graphic — an official-style "ALINEACIÓ" lineup card in club branding, listing starters and substitutes over a posed player photo. Designed team-sheet art, not a news photo.</media>

**Mode performance note:** News Flash is by far the most frequent mode but individually the least impactful; routine updates like fee/negotiation status posts sit around 10k–16k likes. The rare climax posts — a confirmed-deal Breaking post with a composite kit photo, or an endorsement Quote post with a real photo (Guardiola/Rodri) — draw far higher engagement (28k–36k+ likes), meaning frequency and performance diverge: the saga's routine drip-feed sustains the audience, but the escalation-ladder climax posts are what actually spike.

## Repeating Sub-Units

The List Recap and long-form Attributed Quote modes are the only shapes built from a repeated internal unit.

Bullet unit (List Recap): a "▪️" followed by a short factual clause about one aspect of the negotiation, no terminal period, sometimes a trailing space, 3–4 per post:
- `▪️ Barcelona made an opening €45m to Manchester City for Rodri — was rejected `
- `▪️ The bid was NOT a formal one`
- `▪️ City wants €70m `

Quote-paragraph unit (long Attributed Quote): a curly-quoted sentence or two of direct speech, followed by 1–2 trailing emoji, each on its own paragraph separated by a blank line, with #Transfers only on the final one:
- `“All parties involved expect to continue discussing, with Barcelona very optimistic. The relationship between the two clubs is excellent” ☎️⭐️`
- `“This isn’t a situation where one bid is sent, rejected, end of story. There’s a direct relationship. Initial bid being rejected does NOT mean that Rodri is far away or there’s panic” ⏳`
- `“Barcelona expected to continue talking, to come with a new proposal, find a solution for all parties” #Transfers 💼🔵🔴`

## Block Skeleton

For the long-form Attributed Quote mode (the corpus's longest, up to 505 characters):

OPENER EMOJI + LABEL (e.g. `🚨🗣️`) → ATTRIBUTION LEAD-IN naming the source and topic ("More on the Rodri case from @FabrizioRomano:") → QUOTE-PARAGRAPH UNIT (curly-quoted speech + trailing emoji), repeats 2–3 times, each separated by a blank line → final QUOTE-PARAGRAPH UNIT carries the closing `#Transfers` + club-colour emoji instead of a standalone emoji. No CTA block; the post ends on the final quote.

## Post Relationships

Posts run as a rolling live-blog of the same one or two sagas rather than standalone items: the Rodri saga and the Ferran Torres saga each accumulate a chronological sequence of updates that reuse the same fee figures and escalate the same certainty verbs (from "considering"/"studying" → "negotiations underway" → "breakthrough" → "ACCEPTED"). Numbers introduced early (an opening €45m bid) are referenced again in later posts as the baseline for the next figure (€70m demand, €46m revised offer), so later posts assume the reader remembers the earlier figure rather than re-explaining it. A breaking or fast-moving cluster of contradictory reports is often followed within the same session by a Patience/Meta post that explicitly references the confusion ("…and now, there's a media race over who'll be the "first" to report...") and resets expectations without adding new facts — nothing is "upgraded" in these pairs, the meta post exists purely to manage the audience until the next real News Flash lands.

## Formatting

- **Length is trimodal.** Single-line status updates cluster around the median (125 chars): `❗️Barça will not force Ferran to stay. @FabrizioRomano #Transfers 👍🏼☎️`. Very short fragments sit at the low end (p10 38 chars): `How much would you offer for Rodri? 💰`. Multi-paragraph analysis/quote posts stretch to the top (p90 273, max 505); only 2/50 posts exceed 280 characters, and both are the long attributed-quote or analysis-plus-label posts. Do not pad a routine one-fact update into a multi-paragraph post — that shape is reserved for direct multi-sentence quotes or explicit reader-management asides.
- **Line breaks:** default to a single unbroken line (41/50 posts). When breaking, use a full blank line between paragraphs/items, never a single line break (0/50 posts have exactly one break; 9/50 have two-or-more).
- **Emoji:** present in 45/50 posts. Dominant set, in rough order of frequency: 🚨 (opener, escalates by doubling), 🔵🔴 (Barcelona colours, closer), ❗️ (opener for contextual/clarifying updates, lower urgency than 🚨), ☎️/📞 (talks ongoing), 💥 (impact, paired with 🚨 for the biggest stories), 💰 (fee/money mentioned), ⏳ (pending), ⛔️ (collapsed/blocked), ▪️ (bullet marker in recap lists), 👀 (developing, watch this), 🇦🇷 and other flags (player nationality), ✅ (confirmed/agreed). Roughly 20 rarer glyphs appear situationally tied to specific stories (🪑 for a bench decision, 🔥 for a hot confirmation, ❤️ for an endorsement quote, ☀️/☕️/😆/😛 for personal asides) — do not generalize these into a rule beyond the story that produced them.
- **Hashtags:** exactly one, `#Transfers`, appears in 36/50 posts, positioned after the @handle attribution and before or interleaved with the closing emoji cluster. Never stack hashtags, never use a different one.
- **Mentions:** 32/50 posts carry a source @handle; almost always exactly one, occasionally two when two accounts jointly reported (`@Nilsola10 @JijantesFC`).
- **URLs:** 7/50 posts, always at the very end after a grammatically complete unit, never mid-phrase. The one exception is the lineup-graphic post, which ends mid-label on a colon: `🚨 LINEUP: https://t.co/b4aVSvmrHE`.
- **Punctuation:** curly quotes “” for direct speech (4/50 posts), never straight quotes (0/50). Em dash — used mid-sentence for a clarifying interjection (5/50 posts), e.g. "It's not FIFA — you don't just go to a player...". Ellipsis … opens a musing/continuation-of-thought post (4/50 posts), e.g. "…and now, there's a media race..." and "…not sleeping yet, just in case 😆". Colon (26/50 posts) follows structural labels (`JUST IN:`, `BREAKING:`, `To sum things up:`) and quote-attribution verbs (`Simeone tells SER:`).
- **Emphasis asterisks:** a word or short phrase wrapped in single asterisks marks the pivotal threshold in analysis/patience posts — `*really*`, `*at least*` — distinct from ALL-CAPS, and confined to the reporter's own analytical voice, not the news-flash mode.
- **Numerals and money:** currency symbol prefixed directly to the digits, millions abbreviated lowercase "m" with no space (`€50m`, `€4.8m`), ranges given as a slash (`€10m/€15m`), fee spans with a hyphen (`€60m-€65m`). Percentages have no space (`100%`). "+" is sometimes used as shorthand for "and" in analysis posts, and "b/w" as shorthand for "between".
- **Character fidelity:** no misspellings, duplicated words, or inconsistent spellings were found in this sample — write clean, standard English; do not introduce looseness that isn't evidenced.
- **Media dependency:** the lineup-announcement shape is grammatically empty without its graphic (`🚨 LINEUP:` plus link only) and always pairs with an official-style lineup card. The top-tier "🚨🚨💥"-ladder breaking posts about the Rodri-to-Barcelona saga are frequently paired with a photoshopped image of the player in Barcelona kit, escalating in polish as the deal gets more certain; endorsement-quote posts pair with a real, unposed photo of the endorser with the player (e.g. Guardiola with Rodri) rather than a composite graphic.

## Vocabulary & Phrasing

- **"JUST IN:"** — REUSABLE template label, opens a fresh single-fact development immediately after the emoji. "🚨 JUST IN: Roony OUT as well." pattern seen repeatedly, e.g. "🚨 JUST IN: Offers are being heard for Hector Fort."
- **"BREAKING:"** — REUSABLE template label, reserved for bigger confirmed developments, always follows a doubled 🚨. "🚨🚨 BREAKING: Liverpool signs Araujo on loan!"
- **"Be patient."** — REUSABLE standalone closer for reader-management posts during conflicting reports. Appears in "It's not FIFA..." and in the media-race post.
- **"Calm."** — REUSABLE one-word opener for a patience post, followed by a blank line and explanatory sentences.
- **"To sum things up:"** — REUSABLE list-intro label preceding a ▪️ bullet recap.
- **"More follows."** — REUSABLE promise-of-continuation tag appended right after a breaking claim: "Al Hilal made contact with Barcelona for Casado! More follows."
- **"Fab says"** — REUSABLE informal shorthand for Fabrizio Romano, used only in the reporter's own analysis voice, never in formally attributed news-flash posts (which use the full @FabrizioRomano handle instead).
- A drafted post must never reproduce any corpus post in full — the phrases above are reusable *shapes*, not license to republish, e.g., a new draft must not simply resend "🚨🔥 BREAKING: All contractual terms now ACCEPTED by Rodri." verbatim; it must apply the shape to new content.

## Repeating Sub-Units

The List Recap and long-form Attributed Quote modes are the only shapes built from a repeated internal unit.

Bullet unit (List Recap): a "▪️" followed by a short factual clause about one aspect of the negotiation, no terminal period, sometimes a trailing space, 3–4 per post:
- `▪️ Barcelona made an opening €45m to Manchester City for Rodri — was rejected `
- `▪️ The bid was NOT a formal one`
- `▪️ City wants €70m `

Quote-paragraph unit (long Attributed Quote): a curly-quoted sentence or two of direct speech, followed by 1–2 trailing emoji, each on its own paragraph separated by a blank line, with #Transfers only on the final one:
- `“All parties involved expect to continue discussing, with Barcelona very optimistic. The relationship between the two clubs is excellent” ☎️⭐️`
- `“This isn’t a situation where one bid is sent, rejected, end of story. There’s a direct relationship. Initial bid being rejected does NOT mean that Rodri is far away or there’s panic” ⏳`
- `“Barcelona expected to continue talking, to come with a new proposal, find a solution for all parties” #Transfers 💼🔵🔴`

## Block Skeleton

For the long-form Attributed Quote mode (the corpus's longest, up to 505 characters):

OPENER EMOJI + LABEL (e.g. `🚨🗣️`) → ATTRIBUTION LEAD-IN naming the source and topic ("More on the Rodri case from @FabrizioRomano:") → QUOTE-PARAGRAPH UNIT (curly-quoted speech + trailing emoji), repeats 2–3 times, each separated by a blank line → final QUOTE-PARAGRAPH UNIT carries the closing `#Transfers` + club-colour emoji instead of a standalone emoji. No CTA block; the post ends on the final quote.

## Post Relationships

Posts run as a rolling live-blog of the same one or two sagas rather than standalone items: the Rodri saga and the Ferran Torres saga each accumulate a chronological sequence of updates that reuse the same fee figures and escalate the same certainty verbs (from "considering"/"studying" → "negotiations underway" → "breakthrough" → "ACCEPTED"). Numbers introduced early (an opening €45m bid) are referenced again in later posts as the baseline for the next figure (€70m demand, €46m revised offer), so later posts assume the reader remembers the earlier figure rather than re-explaining it. A breaking or fast-moving cluster of contradictory reports is often followed within the same session by a Patience/Meta post that explicitly references the confusion ("…and now, there's a media race over who'll be the "first" to report...") and resets expectations without adding new facts — nothing is "upgraded" in these pairs, the meta post exists purely to manage the audience until the next real News Flash lands.
